children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange pulled back further late Thursday morning, as declines in comparable oils continued to spill over into the oilseed.
Crude oil lost as much as US$2 per barrel on reports a pipeline in Saudi Arabia damaged by Iran-backed Houthi rebels will resume operations in the coming days.
Chicago soyoil gave up more than one cent per pound, while European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil were also in negative territory.

The canola market was moving on from Wednesday's Statistics Canada production report that estimated the 2026-27 canola crop at 22.1 million metric tons. However, an analyst said production, seeded acres and yields will likely be lower in StatCan's survey-based December report.

Thursday is looking like a good day to harvest in the Prairies. Central and southern parts of Alberta and Saskatchewan will be sunny with daytime temperatures exceeding 20 degrees Celsius. Southern Manitoba will also see sunshine, albeit with slightly cooler temperatures.
The Canadian dollar was down two-tenths of a U.S. cent compared with Wednesday's close.
About 28,400 canola contracts have traded at 10:22 CDT.
